case_note: Not cherry-picked. For each held-out test case, margin is the champion fitness minus the best hand-written baseline on that same case (an infeasible score counts as missing). The case shown is the median margin. An even count uses the lower of the two central margins, then the smaller case id. Selected test-49 (margin -0.001040).

policies.label: GeneAI champion
rules_plain: Consider the first 24 waiting jobs.
Prefer jobs with a hard deadline (weight 0.50).
Prefer short jobs (weight 0.24).
Prefer the machine class that matches the job (weight 0.20).
Prefer packing onto already busy CPUs (weight 0.07).
Break ties by deadline, then job_id, then machine_id.

policies.label: GPT-5.5 one-shot
policies.description: Eligibility-filtered composed weighted queue: prioritize short urgent work on feasible low-cost machines, avoid overloaded CPU/memory placements, and apply strong affinity for GPU and high-memory classes.
rules_plain: Consider the first 18 waiting jobs.
Prefer jobs with a hard deadline (weight 0.82).
Prefer short jobs (weight 0.72).
Prefer jobs close to their deadline (weight 0.62).
Prefer lower-power machines (weight 0.58).
Prefer the machine class that matches the job (weight 0.55).
Avoid packing onto already busy memory (weight -0.54).
Avoid packing onto already busy CPUs (weight -0.46).
Prefer machines with free CPU (weight 0.44).
Avoid the next machine in rotation (weight -0.32).
Prefer jobs that have already waited (weight 0.28).
Break ties by deadline, then duration, then machine_cost, then free_cpu.
For gpu jobs, weight the machine class that matches the job at 1.00 instead of the default.
For high_mem jobs, weight the machine class that matches the job at 0.92 instead of the default.

policies.label: Hand-written deadline weighted
rules_plain: Consider the first 36 waiting jobs.
Prefer jobs close to their deadline (weight 0.85).
Prefer short jobs (weight 0.50).
Break ties by deadline, then job_id, then machine_id.

policies.label: Round robin
rules_plain: Consider the first 36 waiting jobs.
Prefer the next machine in rotation (weight 1.00).
Prefer jobs that have already waited (weight 0.10).
Break ties by arrival, then job_id, then machine_id.
